items.title: [Bug] deepep FP8 MoE on GB300/sm_103 crashes in DeepGEMM m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous —   UE8M0 scale-format mismatch (CUDA 719 / smxx_layout.cuh:131 assert)
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


## Summary
On GB300 (sm_103), serving a DeepSeek MoE with the `deepep` a2a backend + FP8 crashes on the **first real request** with an opaque `CUDA error 719 (CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED)` inside DeepGEMM's `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1`, the 719 unmasks to a device-side assertion:

```
Assertion failed: deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/smxx_layout.cuh:131,
                  condition: (values[j] & 0x807fffffu) == 0
```

`0x807fffff` masks the fp32 sign + 23 mantissa bits, so the kernel is asserting the scale factors are **UE8M0** (power-of-two, exponent-only). Instrumenting the call site shows the two operands are in **different scale formats**:

```
a_sf (activation scale) = torch.int32    # UE8M0-packed
b_sf (weight scale)     = torch.float32   # raw, NOT UE8M0
m=768 n=2816 k=2048 num_groups=16
```

No single `disable_ue8m0_cast` reconciles a mixed pair, so the kernel asserts. **This is not a DeepGEMM/hardware limitation** — DeepGEMM's grouped fp8 kernel runs correctly on sm_103 in isolation (see below). It's a scale-format inconsistency in SGLang's Blackwell deepep-fp8 path: the **MoE expert weight scales are not UE8M0-requantized** while the activation scales are.

**Note:** startup + DeepGEMM warmup **succeed** because the warmup uses trivial `torch.ones` scales, which are coincidentally UE8M0-valid (1.0 is a power of two). Only the **first real request** — whose per-block scales are not powers of two — trips the assertion.

## Root cause
`srt/layers/quantization/utils::should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0(...)` gates whether FP8 weight scales get UE8M0-requantized at load. On this path the **MoE expert weight scales stayed `float32`** (the requant did not fire), while the activation-scale path produced `int32` UE8M0-packed scales — so the two operands handed to `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` disagree. This is the same family as #34340 (`is_sm100_supported()` is a `major == 10` check, so sm_103 takes SM100 paths inconsistently).

## DeepGEMM is not at fault (isolation evidence)
DeepGEMM's own tests pass on sm_103 for the exact kernels SGLang uses, with **both** the bundled `0.1.5.post3` and current `2.6.1`:
- `tests/test_fp8_fp4.py::test_gemm` (plain), `test_m_grouped_gemm_contiguous`, `test_m_grouped_gemm_masked` → all PASS, ~3.5 PFLOPS fp8, 0 errors.

So the kernel correctly *rejects* malformed (mixed-format) input; it is not missing sm_103 support.

## Attempted fix (partial — confirms the direction)
Packing the weight scale to int32 UE8M0 per-group and calling with `disable_ue8m0_cast=True` gets **past** the UE8M0 assertion but then hits a layout assertion:
```
Assertion (layout.hpp:97): sf.size(-2) == ceil_div(mn, gran_mn)
```
i.e., packing is **necessary but not sufficient** — the packed weight scale must be in the **mn-major, TMA-aligned grouped layout** (via `get_mn_major_tma_aligned_packed_ue8m0_tensor` / the load-time `requant_block_scale_ue8m0_for_deepgemm` path), not a naive per-group stack. This is why the correct fix belongs at weight-load, using SGLang's own UE8M0 helpers.

## Suggested fix
Ensure MoE **expert** weight scales are UE8M0-requantized (with the correct grouped TMA-aligned layout) whenever the DeepGEMM runner will be used for the deepep path on Blackwell — i.e., make the weight-load requant fire for this path so it matches the activation scale format. More generally (per #34340): `is_sm100_supported()` reads as a capability check but is a family check; SM100-specific format assumptions should be exact-arch aware for sm_103.

## Workarounds
- **MoE serving on GB300 today:** vLLM/Dynamo (do not route through this DeepGEMM path).
- Possibly `--moe-runner-backend <alt>` (as #34340 uses marlin for its trtllm-gen MoE bug) — untested for the deepep path here; SGLang's deepep may not register an alternate runner.

## Related
#34340 (same sm_103 SM10x MoE gating class), #20776 (auto-fallback when scale_fmt not UE8M0), #29993 / #29954 (UE8M0 scale-pack assert family, B200), #29038 (Blackwell DeepGEMM accuracy), #27384 (sibling sm_103 device-assert).

We have full logs and the instrumented dtype trace, and a standing GB300 repro cluster — happy to test a fix.

### Reproduction

Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`, single node, TP=4 / EP=4, deepep + FP8.

Launch the server (device-side assertions on, so the 719 shows its real cause):
```bash
CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --trust-remote-code --quantization fp8 \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal --attention-backend triton \
  --disable-cuda-graph --moe-dense-tp-size 1
```
Server starts and the DeepGEMM warmup completes (`Uvicorn running` / `Application startup complete`). Then send one request:
```bash
curl -s localhost:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"The capital of France is","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":8}}'
```
→ the scheduler crashes on this first request (empty response). Without `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1` it appears only as `CUDA error 719 (CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED)` in `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`; with them, the `smxx_layout.cuh:131` UE8M0 assertion above is shown.

items.title: [Bug] Multimodal CUDA IPC transport auto-selected on WSL2, where CUDA IPC is unsupported — scheduler crashes with no hint at --mm-feature-transport
items.body:
## Summary

On WSL2, any multimodal model fails to start because the scheduler dies in the CUDA IPC multimodal feature transport. **WSL2 does not support CUDA IPC** (`cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` / `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` are unsupported there), but `_handle_multimodal_feature_transport` auto-selects `cuda_ipc` for any multimodal model on single-node CUDA.

The workaround is `--mm-feature-transport cpu`, but nothing in the error output points to it.

## Reproduction

RTX 5090, Windows 11 + WSL2, Docker, image `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b`.

```bash
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 32g -p 30000:30000 \
  -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  --ipc=host lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b \
  sglang serve --trust-remote-code \
    --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \
    --attention-backend flashinfer --max-running-requests 1 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

## Actual behaviour

The HTTP server comes up, then the scheduler crashes on the first request:

```
Failed to deserialize from cached pooled CUDA IPC handle (CUDA error: invalid resource handle
Search for `cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle' in ...
). Invalidating cache entry and retrying uncached.
Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 500, in reconstruct_on_target_device
    ) = self._reconstruct_from_ipc_extra(
  File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 416, in _reconstruct_from_ipc_extra
    storage = _pool_handle_cache_get_or_open(cache_key, redirected_handle)
  File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 75, in _pool_handle_cache_get_or_open
    storage = _open_pooled_storage_uncached(pool_handle)
  File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 66, in _open_pooled_storage_uncached
    return torch.UntypedStorage._new_shared_cuda(*pool_handle)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid resource handle
```

Setting `SGLANG_USE_IPC_POOL_HANDLE_CACHE=0` does not help — the uncached path uses the same unsupported CUDA IPC calls.

## Expected behaviour

Either:

1. **Auto-detect WSL2** in `_handle_multimodal_feature_transport` and resolve to `cpu` instead of `cuda_ipc`, the same way multi-node and PD-disaggregated deployments already fall back; or
2. **Point at the fix in the error.** The current traceback names no flag. A message such as `CUDA IPC is unavailable (common on WSL2). Pass --mm-feature-transport=cpu.` would save a lot of time.

Option 1 seems consistent with the existing auto policy in `server_args.py`, which already narrows `cuda_ipc` to cases where it is known to work.

WSL2 can be detected by checking for `microsoft` / `WSL` in `/proc/version` or `uname -r`.

## Workaround

```
--mm-feature-transport cpu
```

Confirmed working: the server starts, text and vision requests both succeed, and a 190K-token prompt completes without issue. The only cost is routing image features through host memory.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32 GB)
- OS: Windows 11 + WSL2, kernel `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`
- Docker image: `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b`
- Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (multimodal, hybrid GDN)

## Related

Other CUDA IPC transport fallback issues, though neither covers WSL2: #33687, #29687

items.title: [RFC] Orchestrator-facing Elastic EP lifecycle contract
items.body:
## Motivation

Dynamo is designing Kubernetes-managed Elastic EP in [Dynamo DEP #13121](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13121). SGLang's merged scale-up path is already close to what an external reconciler needs: it accepts an absolute EP target, distinguishes effective and pending size, lets joining cohorts wait for admission, and exposes asynchronous status.

To turn that into a reliable Kubernetes lifecycle, the orchestrator must be able to recover after a controller restart or request timeout, identify the joining or retiring cohort for one operation, and know when capacity is safe to delete. The goal is not to standardize SGLang's internal topology; it is to make the boundary used by an external process orchestrator explicit and queryable.

## Proposed orchestrator-facing contract

### Resize identity and status

- Accept an absolute target and associate it with an operation ID or generation.
- Treat a repeated request for the active or in-progress target as the same operation.
- Report a stable runtime instance ID, operation ID, effective size, pending target, documented phase, and operation-scoped error.
- Make it possible to distinguish an engine restart from an operation that is still progressing.

A conceptual status shape is:

```json
{
  "instance_id": "server-7",
  "operation_id": "resize-42",
  "effective_ep_size": 4,
  "pending_ep_size": 6,
  "phase": "waiting_for_cohort",
  "last_error": null
}
```

### Joining-cohort identity

For scale-up, expose enough information to associate externally launched joiners with one operation:

- cohort or operation ID;
- expected rank range and ready-rank count;
- a topology/configuration fingerprint;
- explicit mismatch and timeout errors.

This prevents a stale joiner from a failed operation from being admitted into a later resize that happens to reuse the same rank offset.

### Scale-down and process ownership

For scale-down, separate topology commit from external process termination. The surviving coordinator should report the retired ranks and when they are safe for the orchestrator to terminate:

```json
{
  "phase": "serving_shrunk",
  "effective_ep_size": 4,
  "retired_ranks": [4, 5],
  "safe_to_terminate_ranks": [4, 5]
}
```

A mode where retired ranks quiesce and wait for external termination would integrate more cleanly with Kubernetes than unconditional process exit. If ranks exit themselves, the contract should still define how the surviving coordinator proves the smaller topology committed, because Kubernetes may restart exited containers.

### Machine-readable scale mapping and capabilities

The native API can remain expressed in physical EP ranks. An external autoscaler nevertheless needs a machine-readable mapping from logical serving replicas to physical targets, especially with the DP-attention replica granularity proposed in [#33728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33728).

Useful capability fields include:

- effective and maximum physical EP size;
- logical DP size;
- replica width and target granularity;
- supported scale directions;
- relevant topology constraints or a configuration fingerprint.

For the topology in #33728:

```text
replica_width = attn_tp_size * attn_cp_size
physical_ep_target = logical_dp_target * replica_width
```

## Kubernetes capacity consideration

The scale-down design in [#33111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33111) proposes launching `max_ep_size` ranks and pre-shrinking to the desired initial size. Requiring maximum physical GPU capacity at cold start would limit pay-as-you-grow deployments. If possible, it would be preferable to reserve maximum-sized metadata/buffers while launching only the initially active ranks, then add or recover the remaining slots on demand.

## Related work

- Original Elastic EP RFC: [#22788](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788)
- Merged scale-up: [#30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164)
- Scale-down draft: [#33111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33111)
- CUDA graph recapture: [#33723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33723)
- DP-attention replica granularity: [#33728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33728)

Would this kind of external-orchestrator contract fit SGLang's intended Elastic EP direction?

items.title: [Bug] Quantized lm_head silently produces uninitialized logits with compressed-tensors (ParallelLMHead not dispatched)
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions.
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

A compressed-tensors checkpoint with a quantized `lm_head` loads without error and then emits **uninitialized logits** — every request returns repeated token 0 (`!!!!!!...`).

`CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` dispatches on two layer types and returns `None` for everything else:

```python
if isinstance(layer, LinearBase):   ...
if isinstance(layer, FusedMoE):     ...
return None
```

`ParallelLMHead` subclasses `VocabParallelEmbedding`, not `LinearBase`, so it gets `None` and falls back to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. That creates a plain `weight` parameter, while the checkpoint supplies `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` — which nothing reads. The parameter is never filled, so the head multiplies by uninitialized memory.

It is silent: the server starts, reports no error, and serves garbage.

**vLLM handles this case** (SGLang's file is marked `# Adapted from vLLM`). In
`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py`:

```python
if isinstance(layer, ParallelLMHead):
    quant_scheme = self.get_scheme(layer=layer, layer_name=prefix)
    ...
    return CompressedTensorsLinearMethod(self)

# ParallelLMHead subclasses VocabParallelEmbedding but is handled above as
# a linear; only true embedding lookups land here.
if isinstance(layer, VocabParallelEmbedding):
    ...
```

The adaptation appears to have dropped that branch. Note `ParallelLMHead` already calls
`quant_method.create_weights` with the `LinearMethodBase` signature
(`input_size_per_partition=embedding_dim`, `output_partition_sizes=[num_embeddings_per_partition]`),
so the linear method works unmodified.

This is **not hardware-specific** — the dispatch has no device branching. It reproduces anywhere a
compressed-tensors checkpoint quantizes `lm_head`.

Secondary point: with the dispatch added, scheme matching also needs `lm_head` in
`config_groups.*.targets`, otherwise it raises
`ValueError: Unable to find matching target for lm_head in the compressed-tensors config.`
That is checkpoint-side and matches what llm-compressor emits.

### Reproduction

Any compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `lm_head` is quantized (i.e. not in `ignore`, and listed
in `config_groups.*.targets`):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <compressed-tensors ckpt with quantized lm_head>

curl localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"...","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17*23?"}],"max_tokens":30}'
# -> "!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!"
```

Leaving `lm_head` in the `ignore` list produces correct output, which isolates it to the head.

### Environment

```
Python: 3.12.13
GPU 0: Radeon 8060S Graphics (gfx1151)     # incidental — the bug is device-independent
PyTorch: 2.13.0a0+rocm7.13.0a20260422
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g3f048c80b.d20260513
sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post1
triton: 3.7.0
transformers: 5.6.0
```

### Describe the bug

  ## Environment

  - Device: NVIDIA DGX Spark (1× GB10)
  - SGLang version: 0.5.17/main(commit: 63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c)
  - FlashInfer version: 0.6.15
  - Target model: radixark_qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4
  - Draft model: radixark_qwen3.8-27b-dspark
  - Target hidden size: 5120
  - Draft hidden size: 5120
  - Vocabulary size: 248320
  - DSpark block size: 7
  - Target LM-head quantization: ModelOpt NVFP4

  ## Description

  DSpark fails during CUDA graph capture when the target model uses a packed quantized LM head, such as ModelOpt NVFP4.

  During draft proposal, DSpark computes the base logits by directly multiplying the draft hidden states with the target model’s lm_head.weight:

  local_logits = torch.matmul(hidden, weight.T)

  This assumes that lm_head.weight is stored as a regular dense matrix with the logical shape:

  [vocab_size, hidden_size]

  For this target checkpoint and quantization backend, the logical LM-head shape is:

  [248320, 5120]

  However, the NVFP4 weight stores two 4-bit values per byte, so its underlying packed tensor has the physical shape:

  [248320, 2560]

  DSpark treats this packed storage as a dense matrix and attempts:

  [245, 5120] × [2560, 248320]

  This results in:

  RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied
  (245x5120 and 2560x248320)

  Here, 245 = 35 × 7, where 35 is the captured batch size and 7 is the DSpark block size.

  ## Root cause

  The standard SGLang logits path invokes the LM head through its quant_method.apply() implementation. That path understands the packed weight layout and invokes the appropriate quantized
  GEMM kernel.

  The DSpark base-logits path bypasses this abstraction and directly accesses the underlying packed lm_head.weight.

  This is a tensor-layout mismatch rather than a CUDA graph memory issue. Reducing --mem-fraction-static or the maximum graph batch size does not resolve it.

  ## Expected behavior

  DSpark should use the target LM head’s quantization method when the LM head contains packed quantized weights. Dense BF16/FP16 LM heads should continue using the existing matrix-
  multiplication path.

  ## Proposed fix

  For a valid quantized LM head, compute the local logits through:

  quant_method.apply(lm_head, hidden, None)

  Otherwise, retain the existing dense path:

  torch.matmul(hidden, lm_head.weight.T)

items.title: [Bug] [AMD] torch.compile: "launcher() missing 1 required positional argument: '_grid_2'" in _fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add_kernel on ROCm + torch 2.11 / Triton 3.7
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] I have included environment info and a reproducible case (see below).
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.

### Describe the bug

On ROCm with **torch 2.11 + Triton 3.7**, serving a MoE model with `--enable-torch-compile` crashes during CUDA graph capture. The inductor-generated wrapper calls the sglang Triton kernel `_fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add_kernel` with a launcher signature that is one argument short:

```
File "/root/.cache/sglang/inductor/ls/clspceh7jykmfhmgewaxclhsm5wephjzynssfspbhtuirwleh6uc.py", line 425, in call
  _fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add_kernel_0.run(buf2, buf33, buf11, buf32, 4, 1, 1, stream=stream0)
File ".../torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_heuristics.py", line 1495, in run
  result = launcher(
TypeError: launcher() missing 1 required positional argument: '_grid_2'
```

The exception propagates out of decode graph capture (`decode_cuda_graph_runner.capture_one_shape` → `full_cuda_graph_backend.capture_one` → `forward_fn()`), the scheduler dies, and sglang tears down the process tree:

```
[2026-08-14 14:37:22] Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed.
[2026-08-14 14:37:22] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=8616, include_parent=True, pid=8616
```

The test harness then reports `Server process exited with code -9`, so at first glance this looks like an OOM kill. It is not — the `-9` is the teardown, and the root failure is the `TypeError` above.

### Reproduction

```bash
sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B --enable-torch-compile --torch-compile-max-bs 4
```

on a ROCm 7.2.4 image (torch 2.11 / Triton 3.7, gfx942). Equivalently, the registered test:

```bash
python3 test/registered/moe/test_torch_compile_moe.py
```

Capture reaches ~94% (`Capturing batches (bs=4 avail_mem=23.21 GB): 94%|#########4| 49/52`) before failing.

### Environment

I cannot paste `python3 -m sglang.check_env` because the only stack that reproduces this is a ROCm 7.2.4 dev image that is not published yet (built from #30984). From the CI job:

- `torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2`, HIP `7.2.26015`
- `triton 3.7.0+amd.rocm7.2.0.git89002410`
- Python 3.12
- gfx942 / MI300X, runner `linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang`
- Failing job: `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-rocm720 (linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang, 0)` in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31805806225

### Where it does and does not reproduce

| Stack | `test_torch_compile_moe.py` | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ROCm 7.2.4 — torch 2.11, Triton 3.7, py3.12 | **fails** | `USE_PDL` omitted, launcher signature mismatch |
| ROCm 7.2.0 — torch 2.9.1, py3.10 | passes | verified `{"passed": true}` in runs [31883806448](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31883806448) and [31853160951](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31853160951) |
| NVIDIA (`base-b`, `1-gpu-large`) | passes | `is_arch_support_pdl()` is `True`, so `USE_PDL` is always passed |

The test is registered on both backends, so this is not a coverage gap:

```python
register_cuda_ci(est_time=130, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
register_amd_ci(est_time=1400, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
```

### Root cause

`fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add` only passes `USE_PDL` when the arch supports PDL, in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/elementwise/elementwise.py`:

```python
pdl_kwargs = {"USE_PDL": True, "launch_pdl": True} if is_arch_support_pdl() else {}

_fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add_kernel[(num_tokens,)](
    hidden_states,
    gate_weight,
    shared_output,
    final_hidden_states,
    hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
    **config,
    **pdl_kwargs,
)
```

`is_arch_support_pdl()` returns `False` unconditionally on HIP (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/utils/arch.py`):

```python
def is_arch_support_pdl() -> bool:
    if is_hip_runtime() or is_musa_runtime():
        return False
    return get_jit_cuda_arch().major >= 9
```

So on ROCm `pdl_kwargs` is empty, `USE_PDL` is never passed, and the kernel falls back to its declared default:

```python
USE_PDL: tl.constexpr = False,
```

Relying on that constexpr default is what makes the inductor-generated launcher signature disagree with the call inductor emits. It only manifests through the `torch.compile` path — direct calls to the same kernel are fine, which is why every other MoE test using this kernel stays green.

### Suggested fix

Pass `USE_PDL` explicitly while preserving PDL behavior:

```python
use_pdl = is_arch_support_pdl()
pdl_kwargs = {"launch_pdl": True} if use_pdl else {}

_fused_gate_sigmoid_mul_add_kernel[(num_tokens,)](
    hidden_states,
    gate_weight,
    shared_output,
    final_hidden_states,
    hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
    USE_PDL=use_pdl,
    **config,
    **pdl_kwargs,
)
```

This is a no-op on CUDA, where `use_pdl` is `True` and `USE_PDL=True` was already being passed.

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py` has the identical omitted-`USE_PDL` shape and is a latent second instance worth fixing in the same change:

```python
pdl_kwargs = {"USE_PDL": True, "launch_pdl": True} if is_arch_support_pdl() else {}
```

For contrast, the call sites that already pass it unconditionally (`ops/moe/moe_fused_gate.py`, `ops/attention/decode_attention.py`) are unaffected, and `moe_fused_gate.py` declares `USE_PDL: tl.constexpr` with no default at all, which is the fully safe form.

### Notes on history and validation

A fix in this shape was briefly committed and reverted on a ROCm image branch, on the assumption that upgrading Triton 3.6 → 3.7 would make it unnecessary. The run above shows it still reproduces on Triton **3.7**, so that assumption did not hold.

One practical wrinkle for whoever picks this up: **no currently published stack reproduces it.** NVIDIA CI is green because `USE_PDL` is always passed there, and ROCm 7.2.0 CI is green on torch 2.9.1. Validation therefore needs a ROCm 7.2.4 image (torch 2.11 / Triton 3.7), which lands with #30984. Until then the fix can only be exercised by dispatching the ROCm 7.2.4 PR suite against a locally built image.

### Impact / tracking

Tracking this separately from #30984 because the fix is in a shared Triton kernel rather than in the Docker/CI plumbing that PR changes. Consequence to be aware of: once ROCm 7.2.4 becomes selectable in the AMD PR suite, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small` partition 0 is a deterministic red on that flavor until this is fixed. It is a known failure, not a flake, and it should not be reclassified as one.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 multimodal mRoPE positions are passed to a 1D fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE CUDA kernel
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

On NVIDIA CUDA, the Qwen3.5-family full-attention implementation unconditionally selects `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` when `attn_output_gate=True`.

The fused kernel accepts only one-dimensional token positions (`positions: [T]`) and loads one scalar with:

```python
pos = tl.load(positions_ptr + token).to(tl.int64)
```

However, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B are multimodal Qwen3.5-family checkpoints. Their image/video prefill path supplies contiguous mRoPE positions with shape `(3, T)`, representing temporal, height, and width positions.

Passing contiguous `(3, T)` positions to the current kernel makes it read only the first (temporal) row. Height and width positions are not applied to their assigned rotary dimensions. This silently changes Q/K for visual tokens and can degrade image understanding and GUI coordinate grounding.

The same defect is present in SGLang v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and current `main`.

## Affected checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Immutable revision | Architecture/config | Affected by this bug |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` | [`6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B/blob/6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | [`1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` | [`017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json) | Same multimodal architecture and mRoPE config | Yes |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` | [`207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | Text-only `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, no `mrope_section` | No, not this specific bug |

The affected 27B configs contain:

```json
{
  "architectures": ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"],
  "language_model_only": false,
  "text_config": {
    "attn_output_gate": true,
    "head_dim": 256,
    "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25,
    "rope_parameters": {
      "mrope_interleaved": true,
      "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10],
      "rope_theta": 10000000,
      "rope_type": "default"
    }
  }
}
```

SGLang registers `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` through the same `qwen3_5.py` implementation that contains the fused CUDA dispatch:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L2354-L2366

## SGLang versions reviewed

| Version | Commit |
| --- | --- |
| v0.5.11 reference path | [`612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900) |
| v0.5.16 | [`fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1) |
| v0.5.17 | [`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102) |
| latest `main` reviewed on 2026-08-18 | [`63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c) |

The kernel file has the same Git blob ID in v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and the reviewed `main`:

```text
56d442098c02fa289414fecf0958638dd7906d5b
```

## Source-level reproduction

### 1. The multimodal processor constructs three-axis positions

`QwenVLImageProcessor.compute_mrope_positions()` calls `MRotaryEmbedding.get_rope_index()`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py#L451-L471

`ForwardBatch` documents the result as `[3, total_seq_len]` and concatenates it along dimension 1 before moving it to the model device:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1128-L1132

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1212-L1253

For image/video tokens, the temporal, height, and width rows are different. For ordinary text prefill/decode they are normally equal, which is why text-only accuracy tests may not expose the bug.

### 2. The VLM passes `(3, T)` positions into the language model

The Qwen3-VL wrapper replaces normal positions with `forward_batch.mrope_positions` and asserts `(3, seq_len)` for multimodal prefill:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423-L1453

### 3. CUDA dispatch has no shape or mRoPE guard

Current `main` uses the fused path whenever CUDA and the attention output gate are enabled:

```python
if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate:
    q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(
        positions=positions,
        hidden_states=hidden_states,
    )
```

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1147-L1163

There is no check for `positions.ndim`, `MRotaryEmbedding`, `mrope_section`, or `mrope_interleaved`.

### 4. The selected kernel is strictly one-dimensional

The wrapper documents `positions: [T]`, and the Triton kernel loads only `positions_ptr + token`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L107-L114

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L131-L153

The kernel receives no positions row stride, mRoPE section sizes, or interleaving metadata. For a contiguous `(3, T)` tensor, `positions_ptr + token` addresses only row 0.

## Minimal runtime assertion

On an NVIDIA CUDA machine, add this temporary assertion at the beginning of `forward_prepare_cuda_fused`:

```diff
 def forward_prepare_cuda_fused(self, positions, hidden_states):
+    assert positions.ndim == 1, (
+        f"1D fused RoPE received shape={tuple(positions.shape)}, "
+        f"stride={positions.stride()}, rotary={type(self.rotary_emb).__name__}"
+    )
```

Then launch either multimodal checkpoint and send one image request:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

Expected result with current code: image prefill reaches the assertion with a shape equivalent to `(3, T)`. Removing the assertion silently feeds that tensor to the one-dimensional kernel.

The same assertion can be reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`.

## Why existing validation missed it

The fused CUDA path was introduced by PR #28320:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28320

That PR changed two production files and did not add a fused-vs-native tensor correctness test. Its reported accuracy validation used a text Qwen3.5 checkpoint and AIME26. Text positions have equal T/H/W rows, so reading only the first row is accidentally equivalent for that control case.

## Expected behavior

For two-dimensional mRoPE positions, Q/K must use the configured temporal, height, and width positions according to `mrope_section` and `mrope_interleaved`, matching `MRotaryEmbedding`.

The one-dimensional fused kernel must not be called with a two-dimensional tensor unless it is explicitly extended to implement the same mRoPE semantics.

## Actual behavior

On NVIDIA CUDA with `attn_output_gate=True`, `(3, T)` positions are passed to a `[T]` kernel. Only temporal positions are read, so H/W rotary dimensions are incorrect during image/video prefill.

## Suggested minimal correctness fix

Use the fused path only for its documented one-dimensional input contract:

```diff
-if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate:
+if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate and positions.ndim == 1:
     q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(...)
 else:
     q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_native(...)
```

Also fail fast in the fused wrapper:

```python
if positions.ndim != 1:
    raise ValueError(
        f"fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate only supports [T] positions, "
        f"got {tuple(positions.shape)}"
    )
```

This is a conservative fix. In the current mRoPE scheduler, Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 text and decode positions may also be represented as `(3, T)` with equal rows, so this guard can reduce fusion coverage for those models. Correctness should take priority; a follow-up optimization can safely pass `positions[0]` in paths where equal rows are guaranteed without performing a synchronizing GPU comparison.

The complete performance fix is to extend the fused kernel to accept `(3, T)` positions plus the row stride, `mrope_section`, and interleaving mode.

## Tests requested

Please add a CUDA fused-vs-native test using identical Q/K, norm weights, and RoPE cache:

| Case | Positions | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text control | `[T]` | Fused and native close within dtype tolerance |
| Equal-axis control | `(3, T)`, all rows equal | Either safely reduce to row 0 or use the native path |
| Real mRoPE | `(3, T)`, T/H/W differ | Must bypass the 1D kernel or match `MRotaryEmbedding` numerically |

An end-to-end image grounding regression test would also be useful, but the tensor-level contract test should be sufficient to prevent this silent correctness bug from recurring.

## Scope and current evidence

The source-level shape/semantic mismatch is deterministic and independently reproducible. It confirms a correctness defect in the CUDA path and confirms that Qwen3.8-27B shares the affected configuration and implementation path.

I do not include a controlled end-to-end CUDA grounding A/B in this report yet. Therefore, this issue does not claim that this kernel explains every observed visual benchmark regression; it claims the narrower, directly provable bug that genuine three-axis mRoPE positions are silently processed as one-dimensional positions.


### Reproduction

```
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \
    --port 8000 \
    --tp-size 8 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

### Environment

I use the 0.5.16+cu129 docker.

items.title: [Feature] Workload-Signature-Based Parallelism Advisor for Diffusion Serving
items.body:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Extend SGLang Diffusion's current rule-based `auto_tune` and parallelism documentation with an evidence-producing advisor that selects a legal execution topology from a workload signature and a calibrated benchmark record. The current documentation correctly explains that CFG, TP, and SP split different axes and that more parallelism is not always faster. `auto_tune.py` already makes high-confidence memory/residency choices and can enable CFG/FSDP under guarded conditions. The missing layer is a reproducible way to answer: > For this model revision, device topology, latent shape, denoising schedule, CFG mode, and effective candidate batch, which legal plan has the best end-to-end objective without failing quality or memory gates? This matters especially for short-sequence world/action models. A wider TP degree may amortize well for a multi-candidate batch but regress a latency-first single request because fixed collective and host-dispatch costs dominate. #### Goals - Enumerate legal CFG/TP/SP/FSDP/replica plans from model and hardware constraints. - Benchmark plans end to end rather than rank them from FLOPs alone. - Key recommendations by workload signature, not just model name. - Preserve explicit user configuration as highest priority. - Add a true world-size-one serving fast path where distributed work is semantically a no-op. - Produce a machine-readable calibration report and explain every selection/fallback. #### Non-goals - Moving a live request between TP topologies mid-denoising in phase 1. - Automatically renting/allocating GPUs. - Declaring one plan globally optimal for every batch size or objective. - Replacing existing memory-safety checks. #### Data model ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class DiffusionWorkloadSignature: model_revision: str task_type: str latent_tokens: int num_inference_steps: int | tuple[int, ...] logical_batch: int candidate_count: int cfg_branches: int dtype: str cache_mode: str compile_mode: str device_topology: str @dataclass(frozen=True) class ParallelExecutionPlan: num_gpus: int cfg_parallel_size: int tensor_parallel_size: int sequence_parallel_size: int fsdp: bool data_parallel_replicas: int @dataclass(frozen=True) class CalibrationResult: signature: DiffusionWorkloadSignature plan: ParallelExecutionPlan feasible: bool latency_ms: Mapping[str, float] peak_memory_bytes: int quality_gate: str communication_summary: Mapping[str, float] ``` #### Advisor flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Sig["Workload signature
shape, steps, batch, CFG, topology"] Caps["Model + hardware capabilities"] Enumerate["Enumerate legal plans"] Filter["Static feasibility
divisibility, memory, backend support"] Calibrate["Controlled end-to-end calibration"] Gate["Quality + stability gate"] Rank["Rank by selected objective
latency, throughput, or memory"] Record["Versioned calibration record"] Resolve["Startup/request-class resolver"] Run["Selected serving pool"] Sig --> Enumerate Caps --> Enumerate --> Filter --> Calibrate --> Gate --> Rank --> Record --> Resolve --> Run ``` #### Plan enumeration and static filters Reuse existing legality rules: - total devices equal the product/composition required by CFG/TP/SP/FSDP; - attention heads and sequence dimensions satisfy divisibility constraints; - the model/backend explicitly supports each parallel axis; - estimated resident memory and temporary peak fit the least-free selected GPU; - cache/compile combinations are compatible with the plan; and - CFG parallel is proposed only for models with the required branches. Static estimates only eliminate impossible plans. They should not select the winner. #### Calibration protocol For each remaining plan: 1. launch in an isolated calibration mode; 2. run a complete warmup, separating compile/cold-start time; 3. run repeated end-to-end requests at the exact signature; 4. record p50/p95 latency, throughput, peak memory, stage times, and collective counts/bytes; 5. apply the model's accuracy/trajectory gate; and 6. store environment, code revision, model revision, driver/backend versions, and device topology. The advisor ranks only passing plans. A microbenchmark win is supporting evidence, not a substitute for end-to-end measurement. #### Runtime resolution Phase 1 should resolve at server startup or route between separately launched pools. It should not reconfigure process groups for each request. Precedence: 1. explicit user-provided parallel flags; 2. exact validated calibration match; 3. compatible conservative recipe from pipeline config; 4. existing rule-based `auto_tune` behavior; or 5. clear failure if the model cannot fit safely. The log/metrics record which tier selected the plan and why other candidates were rejected. #### World-size-one fast path The advisor should also make `num_gpus=1` an explicit serving plan, not “distributed mode with degree one everywhere.” Components should expose whether they require a process group for protocol reasons versus useful sharding. When every effective group has size one: - do not wrap the model in FSDP/sharding machinery; - do not issue rank broadcasts with no receiver; - do not construct device communicators used only by multi-rank stages; - return inputs directly from no-op collectives; and - retain only process-group state genuinely required by the server protocol. This is an execution-plan property, not a check of `dist.is_initialized()` alone. #### Suggested integration - Keep current `auto_tune.py` as the resolver/guardrail layer. - Add a separate calibration command under diffusion benchmark/profile tooling. - Store results as JSON with a schema/version and stable signature hash. - Add pipeline-config capability methods for legal degrees and topology caveats. - Add optional startup flag such as `--diffusion-parallel-plan auto:`; exact naming is open for discussion. - Expose `selected_plan`, source, rejected-plan reasons, and calibration digest in startup metrics/logs. #### Correctness tests - explicit flags always override the advisor; - illegal head/sequence/device products are rejected before launch; - exact signature match selects the recorded plan; - different candidate batch/step count does not reuse an incompatible record; - stale model/code/device revisions fail closed to a conservative path; - quality-gate failure removes a plan regardless of latency; - world-size-one plan creates no sharding wrapper or redundant broadcast; - multi-rank plans initialize every required group consistently. #### Benchmark matrix At minimum, calibrate: - logical/candidate batch `1` and one larger production-relevant batch; - CFG serial and CFG parallel where supported; - TP degrees `1/2/4` subject to legality; - one applicable SP degree for long-latent video; - cache/compile modes claimed by the final record; and - single-GPU resident execution when the model fits. Report communication time together with collective count and payload size. “Time inside all-reduce” alone does not distinguish bandwidth transfer from rank-arrival skew. #### Alternatives considered - **Static model recipes only.** Useful defaults, but cannot represent batch/shape/topology crossovers. - **Choose the widest TP that fits.** Can regress short-sequence/small-batch latency. - **Online exploration on live requests.** Risks cold compilation, OOM, and quality variation in production. - **Reconfigure topology per request.** Process-group/model-shard transitions are too expensive for phase 1; separate serving pools are safer. #### Rollout 1. Define report/signature schema and dry-run plan enumeration. 2. Add world-size-one fast-path assertions. 3. Calibrate one model across two batch regimes and publish the artifact. 4. Add startup resolver behind an explicit flag. 5. Extend model coverage only when each recommendation has end-to-end evidence. ### Related resources - SGLang Diffusion parallelism guide: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/parallelism.mdx - Current diffusion auto-tuning policy: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/auto_tune.py - Diffusion distributed state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/parallel_state.py - Cosmos3 pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/cosmos3_pipeline.py - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py

items.title: [Feature] Trajectory-Gated Regional Compilation for Stateful Diffusion Pipelines
items.body:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Connect SGLang Diffusion's regional `torch.compile` support to a reproducible, full-trajectory promotion gate for stateful iterative models. The repository already contains two strong but separate capabilities: - `DenoisingStage` / `CompiledModuleRegistry` can compile full transformers or repeated submodules; and - `compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py` can compare intermediate denoising latents and final frames between a reference and a candidate run. For a stateful video/action or world model, a single isolated forward is not enough to decide that a compiled path is safe. History length changes, cache decisions may branch, CFG changes the observation point, and a numerically small difference can accumulate across a rollout. This feature would turn “compile succeeded” into “this exact compile plan passed the declared end-to-end trajectory contract for this workload signature.” #### Goals - Represent compiled regions and their supported shape/state regime explicitly. - Warm and validate compilation through a complete request/rollout trajectory. - Separate strict tensor parity from model-level output quality thresholds. - Produce a machine-readable promotion manifest. - Fall back to eager execution when a request falls outside the validated regime. - Keep compile disabled or opt-in exactly as current model policy requires; this RFC does not enable it globally. #### Proposed data model ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CompileWorkloadSignature: model_revision: str dtype: str backend: str parallel_signature: str latent_shape_regime: tuple[int, ...] num_inference_steps: int | tuple[int, ...] cfg_mode: str cache_mode: str state_schema_version: str @dataclass(frozen=True) class TrajectoryGate: checkpoints: tuple[str, ...] tensor_thresholds: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]] output_metrics: Mapping[str, float] require_decision_trace_match: bool @dataclass(frozen=True) class CompiledPlanManifest: signature: CompileWorkloadSignature regions: tuple[str, ...] compile_options: Mapping[str, object] gate_digest: str status: str # validated / rejected ``` The manifest is an offline/CI artifact. Runtime does not rerun the full reference rollout for every request; it checks whether the incoming workload is covered by a validated signature and falls back otherwise. #### Promotion flow ```mermaid flowchart TD Ref["Eager reference
fixed requests and seeds"] Cand["Regional compile candidate
same requests and seeds"] Warm["Complete warmup rollout
compile + cache/state transitions"] Capture["Capture selected internal states
and public outputs"] Compare["Trajectory gate
shape, decisions, tensor metrics,
task/output metrics"] Pass{"All declared gates pass?"} Manifest["Write validated manifest
signature + regions + thresholds"] Reject["Reject plan
retain eager path + artifacts"] Runtime["Runtime signature resolver"] Compiled["Use compiled plan"] Eager["Safe eager fallback"] Ref --> Capture Cand --> Warm --> Capture Capture --> Compare --> Pass Pass -->|yes| Manifest --> Runtime Pass -->|no| Reject Runtime -->|covered| Compiled Runtime -->|uncovered| Eager ``` #### Gate semantics The framework should support three kinds of checks without pretending they are interchangeable: 1. **Structural invariants:** same step count, tensor shapes, cache/reuse decision trace, terminal side effects, and output schema. 2. **Numerical trajectory checks:** per-step max absolute error, MAE, relative error, and cosine similarity at named tensors. 3. **Public/task-level checks:** action tolerance, image/video similarity, or another model adapter metric. Some changes should be bitwise exact; others may be acceptable only under calibrated tolerances. Thresholds belong to the model/workload gate, not a global constant. Passing a final-frame metric must not hide a large early trajectory divergence unless the model's declared policy explicitly allows it. #### Full-rollout requirements A candidate must run: - one complete warmup rollout so compilation, autotuning, and state initialization occur; - at least one measured full rollout with fixed per-replan/per-request seeds; - every relevant history-length or latent-shape regime; - cache on/off and CFG serial/parallel variants if the manifest claims them; and - a reset/new-session sequence for stateful models. Cold compile time, warm steady-state latency, graph count, graph breaks, recompilations, and peak memory should be reported separately. #### Integration points - Extend `CompiledModuleRegistry` with a stable region inventory/digest. - Let `DenoisingStage._maybe_torch_compile()` receive a resolved compile plan rather than only global booleans. - Reuse trajectory-capture plumbing from `compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py`, generalized to named checkpoint adapters. - Add a small manifest loader/resolver near diffusion server configuration. - Record fallback reasons in request/server metrics. No model code should read a CI artifact directly. Model adapters declare capture points and quality metrics; the runtime owns signature matching and fallback. #### Stateful and cache-aware behavior The signature must include state/cache schema and mode because `torch.compile` may trace different control flow when a cache wrapper is mounted or when a history-length branch changes. Compiled state must remain request-owned; graphs may not capture a mutable tensor belonging to a prior request. If a compiled region mutates cache buffers, the custom-op metadata and fake implementation must declare those mutations accurately. Otherwise the plan is rejected even if one sample appears numerically close. #### Tests Unit tests: - stable signature hashing and manifest schema; - supported and unsupported shape resolution; - eager fallback on digest/revision/state-schema mismatch; - capture-point registration and missing-checkpoint failure; - mutation/alias checks for state tensors; - no cross-request reuse of captured mutable buffers. GPU integration tests: - eager vs regional compile across a complete denoising trajectory; - first request vs warmed request; - state reset and changing history length; - CFG serial vs CFG parallel where supported; - compile with cache disabled and with an explicitly validated cache mode; - intentional one-step perturbation is caught at its first named checkpoint. #### Benchmark report Each promoted plan should report: - cold compile/warmup wall time; - warm p50/p95 model and end-to-end latency; - number of compiled regions, graphs, graph breaks, and recompiles; - peak GPU memory during warmup and steady state; - per-checkpoint numerical metrics; - public output/task metrics; and - exact workload signatures covered by the manifest. #### Alternatives considered - **Use one forward-pass allclose test.** It misses accumulated drift and state transitions. - **Gate only on final media.** It cannot localize the first divergence and may hide invalid internal state. - **Compile every encountered shape dynamically in production.** This gives unbounded cold latency/memory behavior and no promotion evidence. - **Require bitwise equality for every model.** Too strict for legitimate backend/topology changes; the model adapter must declare a calibrated gate. #### Rollout 1. Generalize trajectory capture and define the manifest schema. 2. Add offline validation for one existing regionally compiled diffusion model. 3. Add runtime signature resolution with eager fallback and metrics. 4. Extend to one stateful world model with reset/history tests. 5. Consider CI promotion automation only after artifacts are stable. ### Related resources - Diffusion denoising compile integration: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - Existing trajectory comparator: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/tools/compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py - SGLang custom-op/compile guidance: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/advanced_features/piecewise_cuda_graph.mdx - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py - Related vLLM-Omni native-step/golden-trace RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5950

items.title: [Feature] Side-Effect-Aware Step Reuse for Stateful Diffusion Pipelines
items.body:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Define a framework-level, side-effect-aware contract for reusing a previously computed denoising prediction on selected iterative steps while continuing to execute scheduler updates and any mandatory terminal state writes. SGLang Diffusion already integrates Cache-DiT and model-specific cache policies, but recent lifecycle bugs show that “skip a transformer call” is not a complete correctness model. Stateful world models may have several independent lifetimes at once: - request-local denoising predictions; - modality-local video and action loops; - conditional/unconditional CFG branches; and - persistent session/KV state updated only by specific real forwards. An approximate step-reuse policy can be safe only if those lifetimes and side effects are explicit. This proposal adds that contract without prescribing one universal similarity metric. #### Goals - Separate reusable denoising predictions from persistent session/KV state. - Let a model define when a real prediction is similar enough to reuse and for how many steps. - Always execute the scheduler update, even when the transformer is skipped. - Never feed reused predictions back into the similarity history as new observations. - Support independent state machines for modalities or branches with different dynamics. - Force designated real forwards when model side effects must be committed. - Make reset, CFG, distributed-decision, and failure behavior testable. #### Non-goals - Replacing Cache-DiT or standardizing one cache algorithm. - Claiming exact numerical equivalence for approximate reuse. - Reusing state across requests in phase 1. - Inferring safe terminal side effects automatically from arbitrary model code. #### Proposed contract Illustrative types: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class StepReusePolicy: policy_name: str observation_point: str # e.g. "post_cfg_velocity" history_size: int max_skip_steps: int force_real_steps: frozenset[str] # e.g. {"first_two", "terminal"} state_scope: tuple[str, ...] # request, modality, cfg_role @dataclass class StepReuseState: last_real_prediction: torch.Tensor | None = None real_history: deque[torch.Tensor] = field(default_factory=deque) skip_remaining: int = 0 real_forwards: int = 0 reused_steps: int = 0 @dataclass(frozen=True) class StepSideEffectContract: terminal_write_required: bool = False write_tags: frozenset[str] = frozenset() ``` The model adapter supplies `observe_real_prediction(...)`, `decide_reuse(...)`, and side-effect metadata. The runtime supplies lifecycle, isolation, metrics, and distributed agreement. #### Execution flow ```mermaid flowchart TD Start["Begin request / modality loop
fresh StepReuseState"] Step["Next denoising step"] Force{"Real forward required?
warmup, no history, terminal side effect"} Budget{"skip_remaining > 0?"} Real["Run transformer"] Observe["Apply CFG, then record
real prediction only"] Decide["Model policy computes
bounded reuse budget"] Reuse["Reuse last real prediction"] Sched["Always run scheduler update"] More{"More steps?"} Finalize["Verify mandatory writes
and emit metrics"] Start --> Step --> Force Force -->|yes| Real --> Observe --> Decide --> Sched Force -->|no| Budget Budget -->|yes| Reuse --> Sched Budget -->|no| Real Sched --> More More -->|yes| Step More -->|no| Finalize ``` #### Lifecycle and isolation rules 1. State is created per logical request and per declared scope. Video and action loops do not share history unless a model explicitly declares that safe. 2. The first observations are real. A policy cannot make a similarity decision from reused values. 3. Reused predictions never enter `real_history`. 4. The scheduler advances on every configured step. 5. Terminal real-forward requirements override every reuse budget. 6. A request error, cancellation, reset, or session change destroys request-local reuse state. 7. Reuse is disabled by default and invalid policy parameters fail at configuration/admission time. #### CFG and distributed semantics The observation point must be explicit. For common two-branch CFG, a policy that compares the final guided velocity should observe *after* the conditional/unconditional merge. A policy that operates per branch must declare two independent states. All ranks participating in TP/SP/CFG parallelism must take the same execute/reuse decision. Phase 1 should compute the decision on the stage's control rank and broadcast a compact decision token, or derive it from replicated tensors proven identical. Rank-local threshold decisions are not safe because a one-ULP difference near a threshold can desynchronize collective control flow. The current Cache-DiT lifecycle issue involving serial CFG and CFG parallel is relevant evidence that reset ownership must be stated once and shared by every execution mode rather than inferred from wrapper placement. #### Integration proposal - Add a small `StepReuseController` adjacent to, not inside, the generic denoising loop. - Let existing Cache-DiT adapters remain unchanged initially. - Expose lifecycle hooks: `begin_scope`, `before_step`, `after_real_forward`, `after_scheduler_step`, and `finalize_scope`. - Add model adapters only for architectures with an explicit observation point and quality evaluation. - Keep persistent session/KV updates in model state; the controller merely enforces declared mandatory real-forward points. For LingBot-style world-action models, one adapter could create separate video and action scopes, compare FP32 post-CFG velocities, and declare a terminal real forward needed to install persistent rollout state. The framework should not embed those model-specific thresholds. #### Correctness and quality gates Required unit tests: - first `history_size` observations are real; - skip countdown is bounded and cannot underflow; - only real predictions update history; - scheduler is called for every step; - terminal write is forced after a long reuse streak; - state is isolated across requests, modalities, CFG roles, and retries; - invalid thresholds/history/budgets fail closed; - all distributed ranks receive the same decision token; - serial CFG and CFG-parallel lifecycle produces the same reset count. Required end-to-end validation: - cache off vs on with fixed seeds; - per-step real/reused trace; - public output quality metric plus internal trajectory metrics; - persistent state/KV equality after the forced terminal write where exact equality is expected; - multiple schedules and request lengths, not only one single-step sample. #### Observability Per request and per scope: - possible, real, and reused transformer forwards; - reuse streak lengths; - similarity/decision statistics (sampled or debug-only); - forced-real reason; - scheduler steps executed; - terminal-write verification result; and - fallback/disable reason. #### Alternatives considered - **A model-local boolean cache.** It cannot express independent modalities, terminal writes, or distributed decision agreement. - **Use only Cache-DiT wrapper state.** Existing algorithms remain useful, but wrapper placement alone does not define side effects and lifecycle for stateful world models. - **Skip scheduler steps together with transformer steps.** This changes the solver trajectory and is out of scope. - **Compare reused predictions recursively.** That makes self-reuse look artificially stable and can extend skipping without new evidence. #### Rollout 1. Land contract/controller tests with a synthetic iterative model. 2. Add trace-only mode that computes decisions but executes every real forward. 3. Validate one opt-in model adapter against full trajectory and public output gates. 4. Enable explicit opt-in configuration; keep defaults unchanged. 5. Generalize only after serial CFG, CFG-parallel, and session-state cases pass. ### Related resources - SGLang Diffusion denoising and Cache-DiT integration: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - Cache-DiT documentation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/cache_dit.mdx - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py - Related CFG lifecycle bug: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35054 - Related exact dependency-aware reuse RFC in vLLM-Omni (different reuse class): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/6238

items.title: [Feature] Batched Candidate-Trajectory Ensembling for Stochastic Action Generation
items.body:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Add a first-class, opt-in execution contract for generating multiple independent action trajectories from one conditioning context, executing the candidates as one physical batch, and reducing them to one served action result. SGLang Diffusion already has most of the lower-level pieces: - `Req.num_outputs_per_prompt` represents multiple outputs; - latent preparation preserves per-request RNG streams and batches the deterministic packing/scaling work; - pipeline stages can expand shared conditioning to the sample batch; and - Cosmos3 is implemented as a composed pipeline with explicit latent, timestep, denoising, action, and decode stages. What is missing is a model/runtime contract that says these outputs are *candidates for one logical prediction*, not independent public media outputs. Without that distinction, a world-action model has to implement sequential sampling or ad hoc aggregation inside model code, and the runtime cannot preserve candidate identity, enforce RNG independence, or measure the benefit of batching. This proposal is intentionally narrow. It does not propose averaging images or videos, and it does not change default `num_outputs_per_prompt` behavior. It adds an opt-in path for models whose public action output has a validated candidate reducer. #### Proposed execution contract Illustrative types: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateTrajectorySpec: count: int = 1 reducer: str = "none" # "none", "mean", or a registered model reducer return_candidates: bool = False seed_policy: str = "per_candidate" @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateGroup: request_id: str candidate_ids: tuple[int, ...] public_output: str = "action" ``` The model/pipeline adapter would declare: 1. which tensor is the candidate action trajectory; 2. whether reduction occurs before or after denormalization; 3. the supported reducer and output dtype/shape; 4. which conditioning tensors are candidate-invariant; and 5. whether video or another auxiliary branch must execute for action correctness. The runtime owns grouping, candidate identity, batching, failure handling, observability, and final response construction. The model owns the mathematical reduction rule. #### Request and execution flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Req["One logical request
conditioning + candidate count N"] Validate["Validate model capability
and candidate contract"] Seeds["Create N independent
request-owned RNG streams"] Shared["Compute candidate-invariant
conditioning once"] Expand["Expand/fan out conditioning
and build candidate batch"] Denoise["One batched denoising path
candidate axis = N"] Action["Model-specific action
postprocessing"] Reduce["Validated reducer
mean or registered reducer"] Resp["One public action result
optional raw candidates"] Req --> Validate --> Seeds --> Shared --> Expand --> Denoise --> Action --> Reduce --> Resp ``` #### RNG and equivalence rules Candidate batching must not collapse stochastic independence or silently change seed semantics. - Candidate `i` receives a stable stream derived from `(base_seed, i)` or an explicitly supplied generator. - `count=1` must preserve the current output exactly. - For a fixed candidate seed list, batched execution must produce the same candidate set as the sequential reference under the model's declared equivalence rule. - Candidate ordering is stable across dynamic batching and output slicing. - Retry/fallback may rerun the whole group, but must not reuse a partially advanced generator as though it were fresh. The existing grouped latent-preparation logic is a useful precedent: it already draws request-owned random latents separately and only batches deterministic work afterward. The candidate path should retain the same property. #### Scheduler and batching behavior Phase 1 should admit a candidate group atomically when it fits the configured execution batch. If it does not fit, the runtime should fail clearly or use a documented sequential fallback; it should not silently truncate the group. A later phase may split candidates into microbatches and aggregate when all slices finish, but the request state must then track: - candidate IDs completed/pending; - seed/generator state per candidate; - partial reducer state; and - cancellation semantics for the entire logical request. Candidate-invariant conditioning should be encoded once where the stage contract permits it. An adapter may use an expanded view or an explicit attention fan-out; physical tensor replication is not required by this RFC. #### Integration points Suggested initial ownership: - request fields and validation: diffusion sampling/request data; - group identity and completion: request/scheduler state; - independent raw noise: `LatentPreparationStage`; - conditioning expansion: pipeline configuration's existing sample-batch expansion hook; - candidate reducer: a small action-output capability implemented by opt-in world-model pipelines; - metrics: candidate count, physical forwards, fallback reason, reducer time, and action-only branch time. The first model integration could be Cosmos3 action generation because SGLang already has an explicit Cosmos3 composed pipeline. The framework abstraction should not contain Cosmos-specific tensor names. #### Correctness and quality gates Required tests: 1. `count=1` is identical to the existing path. 2. Fixed per-candidate seeds produce the same ordered candidate tensors in sequential and batched modes. 3. The reduced action matches a standalone reducer applied to captured candidate tensors. 4. Candidate IDs remain stable when unrelated requests are co-batched. 5. CFG serial and CFG-parallel paths preserve candidate membership. 6. TP/SP output reconstruction happens before reduction when the action tensor is sharded. 7. Cancellation and one-candidate failure do not return a partial aggregate as a valid result. 8. Auxiliary video decode can be skipped only when the model declares it irrelevant to the action output. Quality validation must be model-specific. The framework should report candidate-level and reduced-output artifacts but should not hard-code a universal action metric or assume that a larger candidate count always improves quality. #### Benchmark plan Report, for `N in {1, 2, 4, 8, 10}`: - sequential reference latency; - batched latency and peak memory; - number of physical transformer forwards; - conditioning encode time; - candidate-reduction time; - candidate tensor parity under fixed seeds; and - model-declared action-quality metrics. Benchmark at more than one parallel topology. Wider TP may help the larger candidate batch while regressing `N=1`; the RFC should not encode one topology as universally optimal. #### Alternatives considered - **Keep aggregation in application code.** This forces repeated RPCs or model-specific server loops and prevents the runtime from preserving one logical request/candidate group. - **Treat candidates as ordinary independent outputs.** This loses the reduction contract and makes failure/cancellation semantics ambiguous. - **Always expose raw candidates.** This moves a model-system accuracy feature into every client and expands the public payload unnecessarily. - **Average videos/latents generically.** Out of scope and not semantically valid for this proposal. #### Rollout 1. Land internal types and validation with no model enabled. 2. Add a Cosmos3 action adapter and sequential-equivalence tests. 3. Add atomic candidate-group scheduling and metrics. 4. Benchmark before enabling any default. 5. Consider microbatching and additional reducers only after the initial contract is stable. ### Related resources - Cosmos3 composed pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/cosmos3_pipeline.py - Latent preparation and per-request RNG handling: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/latent_preparation.py - Diffusion denoising stage and sample-batch expansion: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - vLLM-Omni request-selected output routing RFC (complementary output-branch contract): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/6302
