items.title: [Bug] Streaming ASR emits partial-word suffixes at word revisions
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Chunked streaming ASR treats any character-prefix growth as append-only. When a confirmed word is revised to a longer word, the emitted delta can start mid-word: "the cat" → "the caterpillar" emits "erpillar".

Punctuation-only growth is also recorded with an extra space, so "hello world" → "hello world," produces the prompt prefix "hello world ,".

Expected behavior: word revisions emit complete words, and punctuation remains attached to the preceding word. This affects the shared chunked streaming state used by Qwen3-ASR HTTP SSE and realtime paths.

### Reproduction

Model: Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.streaming_asr import StreamingASRState

state = StreamingASRState(
    chunk_size_sec=2.0,
    unfixed_chunk_num=2,
    unfixed_token_num=5,
)
print(state.update("the cat one two three four five"))
print(state.update("the caterpillar one two three four five"))
print(state.emitted_text)
```

Current output:

```text
the cat
erpillar
the cat erpillar
```

Expected second delta: `caterpillar`.

### Environment

SGLang commit: 0111b29 (origin/main at reproduction)
Python: 3.12.14
OS: macOS arm64
Hardware: CPU-only deterministic reproduction; no GPU or model weights are required because the defect is in StreamingASRState.

items.title: [Bug] MLA + fp8 KV: fa3 and flashinfer_mla dequantise the ENTIRE per-layer KV pool every layer, every forward (43.7% of a decode step on DeepSeek-R1 / 8xH200)
items.body:
## Summary

While benchmarking a MegaMoE (NVFP4) MoE backend integration on DeepSeek-R1, we profiled the
decode path and found that the single most expensive GPU kernel had nothing to do with MoE.

On both the `fa3` and `flashinfer_mla` backends, the absorbed-MLA path materialises a bf16 copy
of the **entire per-layer KV pool** on every layer of every forward pass:

```python
kv_cache = self.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id).to(q.dtype)
```

`get_key_buffer` returns the whole per-layer pool, so with an fp8 KV cache this is a full-pool
`fp8_e4m3 -> bf16` dequantisation costing **O(max_total_tokens) per layer per forward** —
independent of batch size, sequence length, and of how much of the pool is actually live.

Measured on DeepSeek-R1-0528 (NVIDIA ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint, fp8 KV cache), 8×H200,
`--max-total-tokens 131072`: one 225.79 µs kernel firing **61× per decode step** =
**13.77 ms per decode step**, with **zero overlap** with any other GPU work — 43.7% of a
31.52 ms step. About 98.9% of the bytes moved are never referenced by the page table.

Switching to `--attention-backend flashmla --page-size 64` removes it entirely while keeping
fp8 KV at full capacity: decode step **31.52 ms → 17.68 ms (1.78×)**, GSM8K accuracy unchanged.

## Affected configurations

All three conditions must hold at once:

1. **fp8 KV cache.** In our case it comes from the checkpoint, not the command line:
   `hf_quant_config.json: {"quant_algo": "NVFP4", "kv_cache_quant_algo": "FP8"}`.
   `server_args` still prints `kv_cache_dtype='auto'`.
2. **MLA / absorbed attention**, i.e. `head_dim = kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope 64 = 576 > 256`
   (DeepSeek family).
3. **`fa3` or `flashinfer_mla`.** With `--attention-backend` unspecified our server selected
   fa3: `Attention backend not specified. Use fa3 backend by default.`

`flashmla`, `trtllm_mla` and `triton` call `get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id)` with **no** `.to()`
and are unaffected.

**Note this is not a config error on our side.** `mem_cache/kv_cache_dtype.py` correctly resolves
`auto` + `kv_cache_quant_algo == "FP8"` into `kv_cache_dtype_str = "fp8_e4m3"`. The fp8-native
branch is skipped **only** because of the head_dim gate:

```python
if (
    self.kv_cache_dtype_str != "auto"   # passes
    and layer.head_dim <= 256           # FAILS for MLA (576)
    and not self.kv_cache_is_mxfp8
):
    ...
    q = q.to(self.kv_cache_dtype)       # the cheap direction: cast the tiny Q instead
```

FA3's own non-MLA path casts the small Q **down** rather than casting the large pool **up**.

## Minimal reproduction — single GPU, no model, no serving stack

```python
import torch
# 576 = kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64 ; +1 = the null/sentinel page
src = torch.empty(131073, 576, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
dst = src.to(torch.bfloat16)      # this is the kernel, once per layer per forward
```

Measured on H200 (torch 2.13.0+cu130):

```
max_total_tokens= 65536  N=37,749,312  grid.x= 73730   113.4 us/call  1.00 TB/s
max_total_tokens=131072  N=75,498,048  grid.x=147458   222.2 us/call  1.02 TB/s
```

`grid.x = 147458` matches the in-server trace exactly, and 222.2 µs vs the in-server 225.79 µs
(1.6% apart). The 65536 case is exactly half, confirming the cost is `O(max_total_tokens)`.

**Full repro:** serve any MLA model whose KV pool resolves to fp8 with the default backend, and
profile steady-state decode. Look for one `unrolled_elementwise_kernel` carrying
`LoadWithCast`/`StoreWithCast`, firing once per layer, with
`grid.x = ceil((max_total_tokens + 1) * 576 / 512)`. Its duration is **invariant to batch size** —
that invariance is the signature.

## Where it is in the source

Verified present in `main` on **2026-08-18** by direct fetch of the raw files —
**four sites, two backends**, all under the comment `# Do absorbed multi-latent attention`,
and **none of them guarded** by any dtype check, helper wrapper, or try/except:

| File | Function |
|---|---|
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py` | `forward_extend` |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py` | `forward_decode` |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py` | `forward_extend` |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_mla_backend.py` | `forward_decode` |

## Measured impact

Torch profiler, GPU activities, 5 steady-state decode steps, concurrency 8:

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| calls per 5 decode steps | 305 = **61 layers × 5** (fires in the 3 dense layers too) |
| duration | 225.79 µs (pstdev 0.41; min 225.02, max 228.22 — one tight cluster) |
| cost per decode step | **13.77 ms (43.7% of a 31.52 ms step)** |
| overlap with any other kernel | **0 of 305**; nearest other kernel 51.55 µs away |
| live KV rows at the profiled instant | ~1,440 of 131,073 ⇒ **~98.9% of the traffic is dead** |

Attribution (no python stack was available — the kernels are replayed via `cudaGraphLaunch`):

<details>
<summary>launch geometry, byte cross-check, temporal position</summary>

- `launch_unrolled_kernel` uses 128 threads × 4 elements ⇒ 512/block,
  `grid.x = ceil(N/512) = 147458` ⇒ `N ∈ (75,497,984 , 75,498,496]`.
  `(131072 + 1) × 576 = 75,498,048` — inside, and tight to one row
  (`131072 × 576` would give grid 147456, not 147458).
- `131073 × 576 × 1 B × 61 layers = 4.289 GiB` = the logged
  `KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.float8_e4m3fn, #tokens: 131072, KV size: 4.29 GB`.
- `LoadWithCast<1>` / `StoreWithCast<1>` ⇒ a dtype-converting copy;
  72 MiB read + 144 MiB written in 225.79 µs = 1.00 TB/s.
- Temporal position, 305/305 with no exception:
  `set_mla_kv_buffer` → **[this copy]** → `flash::prepare_varlen_num_blocks` → FlashAttn.

</details>

## Control experiment

Same server, `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16`, `max_total_tokens` pinned to 65536 for both arms
(both logged `dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 65536, KV size: 4.29 GB`):

| MoE backend | KV dtype | pool | big copies | decode step |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | fp8 | 131072 | 305 | 31.52 ms |
| B | fp8 | 131072 | 305 | 37.00 ms |
| A | bf16 | 65536 | **0** | **17.20 ms** |
| B | bf16 | 65536 | **0** | **22.86 ms** |

The kernel **vanishes** (0, not smaller), on two entirely different MoE backends whose own
totals differ by only 0.08% — confirming this cost is independent of the MoE path.

bf16 KV is only a control: it halves KV capacity at equal memory.

## Workaround (what we ship)

`--attention-backend flashmla --page-size 64` — keeps fp8 KV at **full 131072** capacity and
produces zero such launches:

| | fa3 (default) | flashmla |
|---|---:|---:|
| decode step | 31.52 ms | **17.68 ms** |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 200 q, T=0 | 0.960 | **0.965** (invalid 0.000 both) |

Caveat: flashmla loses fa3's fused `set_mla_kv_buffer_kernel` and uses eager
`cat`/`index_put`/`quant` instead, costing +0.425 ms/step. Net gain still 13.35 ms/step.

## Why this is easy to miss

- It does not crash; it only costs time.
- `kv_cache_dtype` prints as `auto`, so nothing in the launch line hints that the pool is fp8.
- It needs fp8 KV **and** MLA **and** one of the two affected backends, simultaneously.
- fa3 is what the server selects when `--attention-backend` is unspecified.

## Prior art

- **PR #34638** "[MLA] Gather only the batch's KV rows for fp8 paged prefill" describes the
  *same idiom* in its own words ("up-converts the whole per-layer KV pool", "O(pool) per layer
  per forward", 17.76 GiB/layer → ~29 MB/layer) and fixes it via
  `token_to_kv_pool.get_mla_kv_buffer(...)`. It targets `flashinfer_mla_backend.py`
  `forward_extend` only and states **"Decode is not addressed."**
  As of 2026-08-18 its change is **not in `main`** — we fetched the file and both `.to(q.dtype)`
  sites are still present, and `get_mla_kv_buffer` is not called there.
- **PR #7148** "Fix FP8 KV Cache Support in FA3 Backend" (merged 2025-06-25) introduced both
  `.to(q.dtype)` sites and the `head_dim <= 256` gate, with no benchmarks. Two users in that
  thread reported DeepSeek/MLA + fp8 KV being no faster or slower than bf16; the response
  attributed it to in-kernel descale overhead, which does not apply to the MLA path because it
  never reaches the descale branch. **The symptom was observed at the time but never localised.**
We also scanned the last 25 commits touching `flashattention_backend.py` (through 2026-08-18):
none address fp8 KV, the KV pool, dequantisation, or absorbed-MLA performance.
If we have missed an existing PR or issue, please point us at it and close this as a duplicate.

- **Issue #30815** "FP8 KV-cache decode slowdown" (fa3, decode, open) is a **different** defect:
  write-side unfused quantisation in `set_kv_buffer` plus a per-layer Q cast, ~0.4–1 ms/step.

## Possible directions

1. Let the MLA kernel consume fp8 directly (what `flashmla` / `trtllm_mla` / `triton` do).
2. Gather and cast only the page-table-referenced rows, as PR #34638 does for prefill.
   For **decode** this additionally needs a page-table remap and must stay CUDA-graph-safe —
   all our 305 launches carry `graph id 23`, i.e. they run inside a captured decode graph.
   This is presumably why #34638 stops at prefill.
3. At minimum, warn when `attention_backend in {fa3, flashinfer_mla}` and the resolved pool dtype
   is fp8 and `head_dim > 256`. Detection should use the **pool dtype**
   (`token_to_kv_pool.dtype`), never the CLI string.

## What we did not do

- We have **not** implemented or tested a fix.
- We profiled **decode only**; the `forward_extend` sites were read, not measured.
- We did not verify how vLLM or TensorRT-LLM handle this.
- The "43.7% of a step" figure is specific to `max_total_tokens=131072`; the cost is proportional
  to it.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| model | DeepSeek-R1-0528, NVIDIA ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint |
| hardware | 8× H200 SXM |
| parallelism | TP = DP = EP = 8, `--enable-dp-attention` |
| flags | `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.56 --max-total-tokens 131072`, page_size 1, **no** `--attention-backend`, **no** `--kv-cache-dtype` |
| KV cache (log) | `dtype: torch.float8_e4m3fn, #tokens: 131072, KV size: 4.29 GB` |
| image | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.x` (digest `sha256:4a5e481e…`) |

items.title: [Bug] Radix cache `evictable_size()` double-counts shared pages, killing the scheduler at idle
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Surfaced while investigating a KV accounting report from @ApsarasX on #32992; the check there fails for the same reason but is unrelated to that PR's fix.

With radix cache enabled, the idle pool-invariant check in `on_idle()` fails and raises, killing the scheduler. All requests complete successfully first — the server dies the next time it goes idle.

```
ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full]
total=469952, available=96, evictable=470016, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0
```

`96 + 470016 = 470112`, i.e. **+160 tokens (5 pages) more than the pool holds**.

This is not a debug-only path: `SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_IDLE` defaults to `True`, and `_check_all_pools()` in `on_idle()` is not env-gated, so the default configuration raises. No `SGLANG_*` variables were set in the runs below.

## It is a counting bug, not a leak

I instrumented `on_idle()` to walk the radix tree, collect every page referenced by a tree node, and intersect that set with the allocator's free list:

```
[PROBE] tree_nodes=14687 tree_pages=14683 free_pages=3 OVERLAP(tree AND free)=0
```

- Physical pages balance exactly: `14683 + 3 = 14686 = 469952 / 32`.
- `OVERLAP=0` — no page is simultaneously free and referenced by the tree, so there is no use-after-free and no risk of serving stale KV.
- But `evictable` reports `470016` tokens = 14688 pages' worth, while the tree references only **14683 distinct pages**. Five pages are counted more than once, which is exactly the `+160`.

So `evictable_size()` appears to count per node reference rather than per distinct page, while `total` is a per-page quantity. Nothing leaks and nothing is corrupted; the invariant compares two different units.

`--disable-radix-cache` makes the check pass and the run complete cleanly.

## Scope of what I verified

- Reproduced on **Ascend NPU with a dLLM model** (LLaDA2.1-mini, `JointThreshold`), TP=1 and, per @ApsarasX, TP=8 with LLaDA2.1-flash.
- **It appears specific to the dLLM path, not to paged radix in general.** Qwen3-8B (autoregressive) on the same hardware with the same workload and an explicit `--page-size 32` and radix on completes cleanly — `Successful requests: 256`, no idle assertion. One model and one workload, so not conclusive, but it is a real negative control.
- **`page_size > 1` is not NPU-specific here.** `_dllm_page_size` in `arg_groups/overrides.py` forces `page_size = dllm block_size` (32) whenever a dLLM algorithm is selected and radix cache is on, with no device predicate — so a CUDA dLLM run should land on the same code path. I have no GPU available to confirm this, so it is a code-reading claim, not a measurement.
- I have **not** tested SWA / mamba caches.
- I have not found *why* those pages end up with multiple tree references — only that the duplication is on the counting side, not on page ownership.

### Reproduction

Reproduced on `4f51dad1da` (2026-07-30) and `d6c837489a` (2026-08-18) with the **identical** `+160` — 926 commits apart, so it is deterministic and long-standing. In that window `invariant_checker.py` changed only by a refactor (`server_args` → `get_parallel()`) and `radix_cache.py` has no `evictable_size` changes.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <LLaDA2.1-mini> --trust-remote-code \
  --device npu --attention-backend ascend --dllm-algorithm JointThreshold \
  --tp-size 1 --max-running-requests 64 --enable-tokenizer-batch-encode \
  --disable-overlap-schedule --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-backend-decode full \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 12 16 24 32 48 64 --port 31099

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --port 31099 \
  --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix --gsp-num-groups 1 --gsp-prompts-per-group 256 \
  --gsp-system-prompt-len 0 --gsp-question-len 4096 --gsp-output-len 1536 \
  --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 64 --flush-cache
```

All 256 requests succeed (`0` request errors), then the scheduler raises at idle.

`--gsp-question-len 4096` is page-aligned; the correlation with page-aligned prompt lengths was first noticed by @ApsarasX in #32992, where a TP=8 LLaDA2.1-flash run showed `+224` = 7 pages against exactly 7 page-aligned prompts in the dataset.

### Environment

- Ascend 910B3, `aarch64`, Ubuntu 22.04
- page_size resolves to 32: not passed on the command line — the NPU default is 128 (hardware_backend/npu/utils.py), and _dllm_page_size knocks it down to the dLLM block size. On CUDA the default is 1 and the same override raises it to 32, which is why this should not be NPU-specific.
- Model: LLaDA2.1-mini

items.title: [Bug] DSA top-k v2: tie-overflow selection is not exact — silently returns wrong top-k members (follow-up to #30512 / #30645)
items.body:
## Summary

PR #30512 and #30645 fixed the *crash/validity* symptoms of threshold-bin tie
overflow in the fused DSA top-k v2 kernel (all output slots written, no `-1`
inside the valid prefix, inf-boundary handling). However the *exactness* gap
remains, on `main` as of `ea27e3d`: when more than `kMaxNumTie = 2048`
elements fall into the threshold coarse bin, the collect pass keeps whichever
2048 arrive first (`atomicAdd` order — scheduling-dependent, value-independent)
and the exact tie-break then runs on that arbitrary subset:

```cpp
// topk_impl.cuh (main @ ea27e3d, L595 / L618; same in v0.5.15–v0.5.17)
const auto count_eq = atomicAdd(&smem->count_eq, 1);
if (count_eq < kMaxNumTie) [[likely]]
  smem->tie.values[count_eq] = {val, idx};       // overflow: value silently dropped
...
const auto tie_count = min(equal_count, kMaxNumTie);  // select from truncated subset
```

Elements in one coarse bin share only the top fp16 bits — they are *not*
fp32-equal — so the dropped candidates can be genuinely larger than the kept
ones. The kernel then returns indices that are not the true top-k, with no
error or flag, and sparse attention reads wrong KV positions. Note
`count_eq` already holds the true bin population, so the overflow is
detectable for free; it is just not acted on.

This is distinct from the ReLU-degenerate exact-tie case discussed in #30645
(thousands of positions on one exact value — there any subset is acceptable).
Our comparison below is against the `torch.topk` **fp32 score multiset**, i.e.
exact ties with different indices are accepted; the mismatches are real value
losses.

## Evidence on real workloads

GLM-5.2-FP8, 8xB200 TP8, official v0.5.17 image, ~1M-token contexts. We dumped
real indexer score rows (~21 top-k layers x 2 adjacent decode steps = 42 rows
per workload) and compared kernel output to `torch.topk` fp32 multisets:

| workload (1M ctx, batch=1) | rows not exact |
|---|---|
| real model logits (synthetic prompt) | 3 / 42 |
| SGLang source-code corpus | 2 / 42 |
| Gutenberg novels corpus | 2 / 42 |

Additional data points:

- Measured threshold-band candidate populations on these rows reach
  **4.7k–31k** vs the 2048 buffer; on the worst rows the output missed
  **1084–1591 of 2048** true top-k members (measured on the same mechanism in
  the v0.5.15 era).
- In a 32K–1M x batch 1–32 microbench matrix, 9 of 21 cells were not exact on
  at least one of five real-score inputs (64K–512K, batch 2–8 included).
- #30512's own device-side diagnostic corroborates trigger frequency: 41
  overflowing rows within a ~9-minute GLM-5.2 bench (`equal_count` up to 1536
  vs the then-1024 cap).

## Reproduction

### A. Suggested minimal repro (synthetic, no model)

Sketch adapted from our validation harness — construct one row where >2048
fp32-distinct values share one fp16 coarse bin:

```python
import torch
from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.topk import plan_topk_v2, topk_transform_512_v2

N, TOPK, PAGE = 262_144, 2048, 64
dev = "cuda"

scores = torch.full((1, N), -100.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
n_narrow = 50_000   # 50k distinct values inside one fp16 bucket
scores[0, :n_narrow] = 1.0 + torch.arange(n_narrow, device=dev, dtype=torch.float32) * 1e-9

seq_lens = torch.tensor([N], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
page_table = torch.arange((N + PAGE - 1) // PAGE, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).unsqueeze(0)
out = torch.full((1, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)

plan = plan_topk_v2(seq_lens)
topk_transform_512_v2(scores, seq_lens, page_table, out, PAGE, plan)

ref_idx = torch.topk(scores[0], TOPK).indices
ref_phys = page_table[0, ref_idx // PAGE] * PAGE + ref_idx % PAGE
missing = set(ref_phys.tolist()) - set(out[0].tolist())
print(f"true top-k members missing from kernel output: {len(missing)} / {TOPK}")
```

The true top-2048 are the *last* 2048 of the narrow band; arrival order keeps
an arbitrary subset, so `missing > 0` whenever the overflow path is taken.
(Post-#30512/#30645 the output contains valid indices — the failure is purely
exactness.) We will follow up with the exact numbers from a fresh run of this
script on B200.

### B. Real rows

We can share the dumped 1M score rows and the multiset-comparison harness used
for the table above on request.

## Suggested fix

1. **Minimal**: after collect, if `count_eq > kMaxNumTie`, take a slow path
   instead of proceeding on the truncated subset. The counter already exists;
   non-overflowing rows pay nothing.
2. **Complete**: progressive refinement — on overflow, subdivide the threshold
   bin by the next bits of the order-preserving fp32 key (12→10→10 covers all
   32 bits) until the candidate set fits; at full depth, remaining ties are
   exactly equal fp32 values and any subset is correct. We run this scheme in a
   production-shaped kernel: 126/126 real rows exact on the three workloads
   above; the refinement branch is rarely taken so the common path is
   unaffected.

A narrow-distribution regression test (shape of Repro A) in
`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` would prevent
reintroduction.

items.title: [Bug] MoE tuner writes config files the runtime never reads (int4_w4a16)
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions.
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

For `int4_w4a16` MoE, the tuner writes its results to a filename the runtime never looks up, so tuning silently has no effect.

The runtime derives the config key from the down-projection shape — `fused_moe_triton_config.py:284`:

```python
E, _, N = w2_shape
```

The tuner applies an extra int4-only halving on top — `benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py:283-285`:

```python
N = shard_intermediate_size // 2
if use_int4_w4a16:
    N = N // 2
```

For `cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit` (E=256, `moe_intermediate_size` 512) the two disagree by exactly that factor of two:

```
tuner:   Start tuning over 400 configurations to create
         E=256,N=128,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json

server:  Using default MoE kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!
         Config file not found at .../E=256,N=256,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json
```

The tuner runs to completion, reports success, and writes a file — but the server keeps using default tiles. Only `use_int4_w4a16` is affected, which is likely why it has gone unnoticed.

For reference, vLLM's `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` computes `N = shard_intermediate_size // 2` with no second halving.

Suggested fix: drop the extra `if use_int4_w4a16: N = N // 2`.

This is not hardware-specific — the key mismatch is device-independent, though my environment happens to be ROCm.

### Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Tune an int4 MoE model — note the filename it announces
python3 benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py \
    --model cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit --dtype int4_w4a16 --batch-size 1 --tune
# -> "... to create E=256,N=128,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json"

# 2. Serve the same model and note the filename it looks for
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit
# -> "Config file not found at .../E=256,N=256,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json"
```

### Environment

```

ROCM available: True

HIPCC: HIP version: 7.13.26154-92b7431876

sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g3f048c80b.d20260513
sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post1

```

items.title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode.
- [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration.
- [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure.
- [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code.
- [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters.

---

## Summary

Under a long-prefill workload with:

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro
- TP=8
- DP=8
- DP Attention enabled
- chunked prefill enabled
- PrefillDelayer enabled
- one 8-GPU node

an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes:

### Healthy synchronized state

- Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s
- DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep
- `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait`
- average running requests is ~8.5

### Pathological LOW state

- Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s
- within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks
- the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk
- `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay`
- average running requests collapses to ~0.15
- residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply

This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s.

Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency:

- throughput: ~48–68k tok/s
- avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9
- residual batches: ~11–14%

Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress.

The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898.

---

## Environment

```text
SGLang version : 0.5.14
commit         : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb
git log -1     : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246)
git describe   : v0.5.14
remote         : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git
local patches  : no tracked-file modifications
```

The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree.

Hardware / topology:

```text
1 node
8 × NVIDIA B30Z
TP = 8
DP = 8
DP Attention = enabled
MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE
```

Relevant server configuration:

```bash
--tp 8
--dp 8
--enable-dp-attention
--enable-prefill-delayer
--chunked-prefill-size 131072
```

With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is:

```text
131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens
```

Relevant MegaMoE cap:

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512
```

Workload:

```text
input length    : 60000
output length   : 1
max concurrency : 16
num prompts     : 160
ignore_eos      : true
seed            : 1
```

The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as:

```text
16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder
```

The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline.

---

## Reproduction behavior

Representative post-reboot runs:

| Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% |
| LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% |
| LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% |
| good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% |
| mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% |
| LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% |

The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise.

A host reboot did not eliminate the problem.

---

## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence

Using the per-rank counter:

```text
sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"}
```

I computed:

```text
progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t))
```

Results:

| Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k |
| LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k |
| LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 |

The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately:

```text
16384 tokens
```

which is exactly one effective prefill chunk.

`realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution.

### Metric-cadence validation

I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk.

Across all ranks:

```text
jump interval p50 = 1.397 s
jump interval p95 = 1.535 s
min interval       = 0.401 s
```

Jump-size distribution:

```text
16384 ×112   (one full chunk)
11264 ×8     (tail chunks)
256   ×3     (small startup fragments)
32768 ×0     (no two-chunk merge observed)
```

Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run.

---

## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW

I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload.

| Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% |
| good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% |
| mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% |
| LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** |
| LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% |
| LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% |

The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run:

```text
18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18
```

All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s.

Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state.

Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch.

---

## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs

From:

```text
sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total
```

healthy runs eventually converge to sustained:

```text
input_estimation="all"
output_reason="no_wait"
```

while LOW runs remain dominated by:

```text
input_estimation="mixed"
output_reason="delay"
```

In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state.

In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime.

I use:

```text
all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay)
```

only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode.

The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model.

---

## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer

I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled.

| Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s |
| 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s |
| 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s |
| 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s |
| 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s |
| 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s |

Mean throughput:

```text
58,980 tok/s
CV = 12.88%
```

The important mechanism difference is:

```text
PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5
PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15
PrefillDelayer OFF         : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9
```

Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime.

This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above.

---

## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse

As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to:

```text
2 requests/s, fixed interval
```

while keeping concurrency=16.

This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful.

Representative results:

```text
burst: 94,630 tok/s
ramp : 53,449 tok/s

burst: 64,016 tok/s
ramp : LOW again
```

The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state.

This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase.

Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration.

---

## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes

I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes.

### 1. #29898 — missing locally

The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch:

```python
prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0
if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1:
    ...
    output_reason="delay"
else:
    ...
    output_reason="wait_timeout"
```

but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true:

```python
if slot_condition or queue_condition:
    ...
    next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count()
    return _NegotiateOutput(
        output_allow=False,
        output_reason="delay",
        ...
    )
```

with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound.

This confirms that the local tree predates #29898.

However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`.

Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse.

---

### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement

The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths:

```text
add_one_req_ignore_eos()  -> negotiation after budget/admission checks
add_one_req()             -> negotiation at the beginning of the function
```

The dispatch condition is:

```python
if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True):
    return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req)
```

This reproduction has:

```text
ignore_eos = true
radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false
```

so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`.

In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with:

```python
if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and (
    not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill(
        local_prefillable=True,
        running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(),
        max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs,
        max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests,
        waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len,
    )
):
    return AddReqResult.OTHER
```

before later request / chunk / admission checks.

Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics.

This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal.

That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger.

---

### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present

The local scheduler already contains an early guard:

```python
if (
    self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0
    and self.chunked_req is None
    ...
):
```

but the later waiting-queue loop still contains:

```python
if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs):
    self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True
```

while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses:

```python
min(
    pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs,
    req_to_token_pool.available_size(),
)
```

where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`.

This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295.

I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor.

---

### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation

The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization.

With the current settings:

```text
disable_overlap_schedule = false
SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false
```

PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path.

Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround.

If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further.

---

### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics

This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills.

The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match.

It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior.

---

## Current interpretation

The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence:

```text
formal workload begins
        ↓
DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts
        ↓
within the first few seconds,
per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount
        ↓
PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states
        ↓
mixed/delay persists
        ↓
under-filled / residual batches increase
        ↓
running concurrency collapses
        ↓
LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining
```

One causal distinction is still unresolved:

### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence

One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer:

```text
same/similar forward opportunity
        ↓
one rank completes later
        ↓
prefill progress diverges
        ↓
Delayer subsequently observes mixed
```

### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression

The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities:

```text
scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges
        ↓
Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions
        ↓
those ranks do less forward work
        ↓
prefill progress diverges
```

I am instrumenting:

```text
sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"}
```

together with:

```text
sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category}
```

using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`.

The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state.

The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between:

```text
Δprefill_progress
and
Δcompleted_forward_execution_time
```

over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence.

Roughly:

```text
ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower
→ rank likely completed less forward work
→ supports scheduler/readiness-side cause

ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher
→ rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress
→ supports execution-duration-side cause
```

This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above.

---

## Why I think this deserves a separate issue

I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together:

```text
DP Attention
+ PrefillDelayer
+ chunked long-prefill workload
+ same deterministic configuration
+ healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state
+ LOW dominated by mixed/delay
+ avg running collapsing near zero
+ rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk
+ request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction
```

#29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug.

The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode.

---

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer?

2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks?

3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state?

4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`?

5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing?

---

## Additional data available

I retained:

- per-run server logs
- per-rank Prefill batch logs
- `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces
- 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures
- per-rank `realtime_tokens_total`
- PrefillDelayer outcome counters
- queue/running-request counters
- host/GPU telemetry
- good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts

I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

In PD disaggregation mode, external routers attach PD coordination metadata (`bootstrap_host`, `bootstrap_port`, `bootstrap_room`) to inference request bodies. The OpenAI path (`/v1/chat/completions`) accepts these fields via `ChatCompletionRequest` and PD works as expected.

The Anthropic path (`/v1/messages`) does not preserve this metadata. Requests are parsed as `AnthropicMessagesRequest` (which has no PD routing fields), then converted to `ChatCompletionRequest` in `AnthropicServing._convert_to_chat_completion_request()` using only Anthropic-native fields. As a result, `bootstrap_room` (and related PD fields) are dropped before the request enters the existing PD disaggregation flow.

On the decode worker, this surfaces as:

`Invalid request: Disaggregated request received without bootstrap room id`

The same request body with the same bootstrap fields succeeds on `/v1/chat/completions`.

Note: `/v1/messages/count_tokens` is unaffected because it only tokenizes locally and does not enter the PD generation/KV-transfer path.

This appears related to the fix proposed in #33076.

### Reproduction

# Prefill
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/model \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 9100 \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
# Decode
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/model \
  --disaggregation-mode decode \
  --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 9100 \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001

# Shared PD fields
{
  "bootstrap_host": "<prefill_host_ip>",
  "bootstrap_port": 9100,
  "bootstrap_room": 123456789
}

# Test 1 — OpenAI works
curl -s -X POST "http://<decode_host>:30001/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "<model_name>",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    "max_tokens": 32,
    "stream": false,
    "bootstrap_host": "<prefill_host_ip>",
    "bootstrap_port": 9100,
    "bootstrap_room": 123456789
  }'

Expected: HTTP 200, normal completion.

# Test 2 — Anthropic fails (same bootstrap fields)
curl -s -X POST "http://<decode_host>:30001/v1/messages" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "<model_name>",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    "max_tokens": 32,
    "stream": false,
    "bootstrap_host": "<prefill_host_ip>",
    "bootstrap_port": 9100,
    "bootstrap_room": 123456789
  }'

Actual:
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "BadRequestError",
    "message": "Invalid request: Disaggregated request received without bootstrap room id. req.rid='...'"
  }
}

items.title: [Tracking] Host allocator: page-aligned allocation with host-side bookkeeping
items.body:
## Motivation

The KV allocator keeps its source of truth on device. Freeing KV therefore reads
device state back -- `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` with a data-dependent
output shape, and on the SWA side the `full_to_swa_index_mapping` gather plus its
`> 0` liveness filter -- each forcing a stream synchronization on the scheduler's
stream. Under the overlap scheduler these syncs queue behind the WAR barrier, so
the CPU parks until the in-flight forward drains. On workloads where requests
finish every step (e.g. PD decode), this is a measurable throughput loss.

None of that information needs a device read: it is host-known at allocation
time. Target design (validated end-to-end by the #31335 spike):

- Allocation is planned host-side in whole pages; each request tracks a
  page-ceiled allocated extent (`req.kv.kv_allocated_len`) with a single writer.
- `free()` receives whole pages by construction -- no dedup, no liveness filter,
  no data-dependent shapes. `torch.unique` survives only behind a legacy API for
  truly scattered index sets.
- Device tables (`req_to_token`, `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, `free_pages`)
  become write-only projections consumed by kernels; the scheduler never reads
  them back.

## Prior work

**Landed**
- #29427 / #29429 / #29432 -- `req.kv` container: owned-KV lifecycle and
  bookkeeping coupled to real allocations
- #32701 -- free KV pages by segment in the paged allocator without a device
  sync (non-SWA)
- #33475 / #34067 -- free-group batching and aliasing fix (hardening the
  deferred-free machinery the sync-free path relies on)

**Closed**
- #31335 (with CI companion #31194) -- the original spike validating the full
  shape
- #25500 -- early PoC: unify page allocation estimation on `kv_allocated_len`
- #33907 / #34783 -- SWA free without a device sync via segment liveness
  contracts; closing in favor of the host-bookkeeping approach (the
  `swa_alive_from` contract only holds on the chunk-cache path; page-aligned
  extents remove the need for it)

## In flight

- #35265 -- page-align the DFLASH decode KV reservation (toward the invariant:
  every writer keeps `kv_allocated_len` page-aligned)
- #35286 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor at PD decode prealloc
  (I2: SWA liveness boundary invariant)
- #35382 -- share the page-aligned decode alloc lens between EAGLE and DFLASH
  (dedup; the watermark loop becomes the single writer of kv_allocated_len)

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 indexer's context-proportional logits allocation is unaccounted by mem_fraction_static — deterministic OOM on long-context prefill
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion.
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

The DeepSeek-V4 sparse indexer allocates a **`[chunk_tokens, aligned_c4_len]` fp32 logits tensor per layer per prefill chunk**, host-side inside sgl-deep-gemm before kernel launch (`csrc/apis/attention.hpp:398`, `torch::empty` through the caching allocator). The allocation grows linearly with accumulated context and is **invisible to `mem_fraction_static`** — no part of the memory budgeter accounts for it — so any sufficiently long prefill deterministically OOMs mid-request, on every TP rank simultaneously (the indexer is replicated, not TP-sharded).

**Repro** (100% deterministic): 4×H100 TP4, `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu129`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.9 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --moe-runner-backend marlin --context-length 1000000`. Single `/v1/completions` request with a ~800K-token unique-text prompt:

```
indexer.py:961 forward → indexer.py:774 forward_c4_indexer
→ deep_gemm fp8_paged_mqa_logits → tvm.error.InternalError:
CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.42 GiB (GPU 3; 1.17 GiB free; 72.47 GiB allocated by PyTorch)
```

The arithmetic pins the buffer exactly: `4096 rows × align(ceil(372K/4/256)·64·4, 256)·4 B = 1.4219 GiB` — the request died at the prefill chunk covering ≈372K raw tokens; the final chunk would have needed 3.05 GiB. A 399,732-token request succeeded (peak transient ≈1.53 GiB happened to fit); the growth law `chunk_tokens × c4_len × 4` is the invariant. At the default `chunked-prefill-size 8192` the non-paged path allocates ~2× per context and hits the same wall around 186K tokens. Current main is unchanged.

### The defect, precisely

- `mem_fraction_static` sizes weights + KV pools only; the only activation heuristic is context-length-independent.
- The sibling **DSA (V3.2) indexer in the same tree already solves this** — it chunks this exact tensor under a free-memory budget (`_should_chunk_mqa_logits`, `SGLANG_DSA_MQA_LOGITS_FREE_MEM_FRACTION`, dsa_indexer.py). The DSV4 indexer has no equivalent on either the paged or non-paged path.
- vLLM (main) treats the same buffer as a first-class budget item: chunks under `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` (default 512 MB) *and* allocates that worst case during the profiling run so the KV budgeter reserves it.

### Proposed fix

Mirror the in-tree DSA precedent in `dsv4/indexer.py::forward_c4_indexer`: chunk logits + top-k over query rows under a free-memory budget (everything involved is row-sliceable; per-slice DeepGEMM schedule metadata is cheap to rebuild), and have `_get_nonpaged_indexer_plan` decline oversized work so it falls through to the chunked paged path. PR incoming from this account — validated on the 800K reproducer above.

Interim operator mitigation: lower `--chunked-prefill-size` (allocation is linear in it) or lower `mem_fraction_static` — but the requirement grows without bound in context length, so headroom-based fixes just move the wall.

Related: #34718 (different defect in the same subsystem — that one is an illegal-address in the top-k v2 streaming band at decode; this one is a host-side torch OOM at prefill; see our diagnosis comment there).

### Environment

sglang v0.5.17 (cu129 image), DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 @ 7872f01b, 4×H100 SXM 80GB, TP4, CUDA 12.9 driver, single node.

items.title: [Bug] NIXL/UCX prefill segfault (nixlUcxSharedThread -> cuEventQuery) is not fixed — reproduces on v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200; #23489 and #23499 were closed without a root cause
items.body:
## Summary

The NIXL/UCX prefill segfault reported in #23489 and #23499 is **not fixed**. Both issues were
closed without a root cause — #23489 same-day as "Resolved via rebase", #23499 with no linked PR or
commit — and #23499 already has an unanswered 2026-07-07 comment from someone hitting it again on a
different GPU/CUDA/SGLang combination.

We reproduce it today on **v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200 x86**, and we have traced it to a missing
CUDA context in NIXL's UCX progress thread. Filing separately here because SGLang's
`num_threads = 8` choice for prefill is what exposes every NIXL PD user to it, while decode's `0`
makes decode immune.

Upstream issue: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/2102

## Reproduction

Production 8×B200 host, both roles co-located:

- prefill: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 0-3, decode: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 4-7
- `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`
- `nixl` / `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp`, `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n`
- image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130`

**9 prefill crashes in 43 hours** of steady traffic, ~one every 4.8h, evenly spread across the
clock — not tied to load, deploys, or any request shape. The decode role, on the same host with the
same image, UCX env and traffic, has **never** crashed.

## Stack — identical every time

```
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

  File "<unknown>", line 0, in cuEventQuery
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in uct_cuda_base_iface_event_fd_arm
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in ucp_worker_arm
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxWorker::arm() const
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxSharedThread::run()
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in __clone
```

## A debugging note that cost us time

`faulthandler` dumps **every** thread, and the Python main-thread frame is different on every
crash — we saw `deepseek_v4_backend.init_compression_metadata`, `mem_cache/allocator/swa.free_swa`,
`forward_batch_info.init_new`, `scheduler_components/dp_attn.all_gather`, and
`utils/common.broadcast_pyobj` across nine dumps of the same bug. All of those are innocent
bystanders. Only the C++ frames matter, and they never change.

Likewise the `Scheduler hit an exception: ... RuntimeError: [gloo] ... Connection reset by peer`
tracebacks that follow are the surviving DP ranks reacting to a dead peer, not the fault. #23499's
original report made the same observation.

Anyone triaging a report like this should grep the dump for `nixlUcxSharedThread`, not for the
scheduler frames.

## Root cause

`nixlUcxSharedThread::run()` (nixl `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_backend.cpp:339`) calls `worker->arm()`
without ever establishing a CUDA context on that thread. `arm()` reaches UCX's `cuda_copy`
transport, which calls `cuEventQuery` and segfaults. NIXL's UCX plugin contains **no** CUDA context
management at all — a repo-wide grep for `vramApplyCtx|pthrCudaCtx|cuCtxSetCurrent` hits only
`src/plugins/libfabric/`, which received exactly this fix in ai-dynamo/nixl#1157.

## Why prefill only

`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`:

```python
num_threads = 8 if disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL else 0
```

and in nixl `ucx_backend.cpp:763`, the shared progress thread is only constructed when the UCX
backend receives `num_threads > 0`. So prefill gets `nixlUcxSharedThread` and decode does not,
which matches our 9-vs-0 crash split exactly.

## Workaround (confirmed at the source level, running it now)

```bash
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS='{"num_threads":"0"}'
```

The `setdefault` in `conn.py` means an explicit value wins, and `num_threads=0` makes NIXL skip
`nixlUcxThreadPoolEngine` entirely, so the crashing thread never exists.

## Asks

1. **Reopen #23499.** It was closed without a fix and its 2026-07-07 follow-up is still unanswered.
2. **Document `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS`** in
   `docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.md`. It was added in #24169 but the PD docs only
   mention `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND`, so the only workaround for this crash is currently
   undiscoverable without reading `environ.py`.
3. **Reconsider the hardcoded `num_threads = 8` for prefill**, or at minimum make it a documented,
   overridable knob with a note about this failure mode, until the NIXL fix lands.

items.title: [Bug] sgl-model-gateway fails Clippy due to needless borrows in cache-aware policy tests
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


Running the same Clippy command used by the `sgl-model-gateway` CI fails on the latest `main` branch because two cache-aware policy tests pass a borrowed temporary `String` to `BasicWorkerBuilder::new`.

Both occurrences trigger `clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args`, and CI treats Clippy warnings as errors with `-D warnings`:

```text
error: the borrowed expression implements the required traits
   --> src/policies/cache_aware.rs:682:41
    |
682 |                 BasicWorkerBuilder::new(&format!("http://w{}:8000", j))
    |                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

error: the borrowed expression implements the required traits
   --> src/policies/cache_aware.rs:741:41
    |
741 |                 BasicWorkerBuilder::new(&format!("http://w{}:8000", j))
    |                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

The expected result is that the gateway's documented CI lint command completes without warnings.

The proposed fix is to pass the owned `String` directly at both call sites:

```rust
BasicWorkerBuilder::new(format!("http://w{}:8000", j))
```

This is a mechanical lint fix and should not change behavior.

### Reproduction


Starting from commit `a2e88279c` on `origin/main`:

```bash
cd sgl-model-gateway
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

Clippy reports `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` at lines 682 and 741 of `src/policies/cache_aware.rs` and exits unsuccessfully.


### Environment


```text
OS: Ubuntu Linux x86_64
SGLang commit: a2e88279c (origin/main)
rustc 1.90.0 (1159e78c4 2025-09-14)
cargo 1.90.0 (840b83a10 2025-07-30)
clippy 0.1.90 (1159e78c47 2025-09-14)
```

No model, GPU, or CUDA environment is involved; the issue is reproduced by the Rust lint command alone.
